references.text: The parallel account in Numbers describes how the spies brought back fruit from the land, including a cluster of grapes from the Valley of Eshkol, and reported to the people about the land flowing with milk and honey.
Joshua and Caleb confirm that the land is exceedingly good and that the Lord will give it to Israel—the same message given in Deuteronomy 1:25 that the land is good.
God's original promise to lead Israel to a good and spacious land flowing with milk and honey, confirming that the land the Lord gives them is good.
The Lord describes the promised land as a land flowing with milk and honey, emphasizing that the land is good just as the spies reported.
Ezekiel refers to the promised land as a land flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands—a confirmation that the land the Lord gives is good.
The Lord confirms the promise to give the land to Israel, as it was promised and reported by the spies as a good land.
The psalm refers to how Israel despised the pleasant land and did not believe in the Lord's word, despite the spies' report about the good land.
